_readme: QUERY-ARBITRATION GATE — cases. See README.md in this directory.
Every case asserts BOTH halves: what the arbitration did AND what it did not do.
expect=served-existing : search served a card AND that card is in the accept set.
Serving a DIFFERENT card is `served-wrong` — a FAIL, not a pass.
expect=generated       : search DECLINED (best === null) AND the model-free route says
`grounded`, i.e. the query reaches generation.
expect=gap             : search declined AND the route says gap — and NOT offdomain.
expect=offdomain       : search declined AND the route says offdomain — and NOT gap.
Accept sets are pinned THREE ways, all reproducible from packages/mobile/assets/data/cards.db:
acceptIds  — an explicit id list, used where the answer is narrow.
acceptRule — {topic: <regex>, domain?: <DOMAIN>} matched against the card's own `topic`
and `title_en`, materialised into an id list at run time. The runner prints
the resulting count so an accept set that silently empties is visible.
acceptProse — {lang, all: [<regex>...]} matched against the CARD'S OWN BODY TEXT — for answers
that live only in the prose (ffct-35303's text IS 'How hot is a single bolt of
lightning?' while its topic is just 'Weather/Lightning').
`accept=N` in the notes below is the count that materialised on the r2 baseline run (2026-08-31);
the runner prints the live count next to every result, so drift is visible rather than assumed.
`why` is the corpus evidence, never intuition: each one names the card or the fact that
settles the expectation. `no card` was established by BOTH a topic/terms probe AND a LIKE
over card prose in en+tl+bis; generated-vs-gap was then decided by the 50,279-row fact bank.
r2 additions:
configLang   — the APP's configured language (default 'tagalog'). LocalEngine.answerQuery takes its retrieval
language from config.language, NOT from the query, so `lang` alone modelled a setting that only
exists if the child switched the app. Three verdicts move on this.
acceptProse  — accept set materialised from the CARD'S OWN PROSE (all regexes must match card_text.<lang>), for
answers that live in the body text and never in the topic/title (how hot lightning is).
aspirational — the expectation is right for the PRODUCT but unreachable for the current machinery (it would need a
concept-level coverage check). Reported separately and EXCLUDED from the green condition, so the
gate cannot silently demand an unbuilt feature.
searchDuplicateOf — this sentence reduces to the same token set as that term case, so the two are the SAME test
for the search half. Excluded from the by-form table; still earns its place on the model-free half.
buckets `chitchat` (decline politely OR teach the science the child named — never a random card) and
`tokenisation` (a compound split or joined, which is not a spelling error and must not be filed as one).
Accept regexes carry their own anchors. Unanchored, /rock/ matched 38 ROCKET cards, /nail/ matched 130 SNAIL
cards, /mayon/ matched mayonnaise and /pulse/ matched nerve impulses — a wrong card would have scored PASS, the
exact failure this gate exists to make visible. A LEADING \b is added only where the stem has a false friend:
\bvolcan would throw away nine legitimate stratovolcano cards and \bgravity\b throws away gravity_tool.

acceptRule.topic: photosynthes|plants make (their )?(own )?food|chlorophyll|plants take in carbon dioxide

cases.why: Child spelling NAMED IN THE RagStore SOURCE ('photosinthesis .589-.601') and genuinely out of vocabulary (df 0), which is the point: it replaces `fotosintesis`, whose df is 1 in the card index — that string is a one-card token, so search served it at 1.000 by construction and the case could never fail. HARD RULE: offdomain here is telling a child their science question is not science. accept=116

A compound typed as two words — both halves ARE in the vocabulary, unlike the Cebuano case, so the query stays reachable. REGRESSION PROTECTION: correct today (serves a Seismic Waves card at 1.000) and a tightening that starts demanding whole-compound matches would break it. accept=220

A Cebuano compound split in two. RE-FILED out of `misspelling`: the failure mechanism is not orthography but a HIGH-FREQUENCY FUNCTION WORD — the surviving token `kasing` is also the Cebuano comparative particle (kasing-bug-at = 'as heavy as') with df 130, which is why search answers with 'how heavy is a blue whale tongue' at 1.000. Nothing about spelling can fix this one. accept=160
